title: CA-GPT, a DeepSeek-based model on an AI-OCT system led by Tangdu Hospital, agrees with expert PCI plans more than ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians in a 96-patient single-center preprint
summary: In a preprint on 96 patients, CA-GPT, built on DeepSeek-R1, agreed with expert stent plans more often than junior physicians and ChatGPT-5, which received only extracted measurements.
account: An arXiv preprint of 11 December 2025 (Fang et al., last author Yan Li) reports the single-center COMPARE study. The study was retrospective and covered patients treated at Tangdu Hospital between June 2024 and August 2025. It compared CA-GPT, “a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system”, with ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) guided by optical coherence tomography (OCT). The preprint states that the large model layer is built on DeepSeek-R1 with 14 billion parameters. Its Methods describe retrieval from more than 100,000 annotated PCI cases and clinical guidance. The authors thank Vivolight Medtech for interface support and training. Decisions for 96 patients were scored against an expert-derived record. In pre-PCI planning CA-GPT's median agreement was 5 against 3 for ChatGPT-5 and 4 for junior physicians. It “showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01)”. CA-GPT received raw OCT images through its integrated pipeline, whereas ChatGPT-5 received manually extracted measurements. The comparison therefore combines differences in models, retrieval and input processing. The OECD Monitor pairs this study with a Xinhua report of 13 December 2025 on the “Titian” ablation robot at Shaoxing People's Hospital. That report describes teleoperation and no AI function. Machine Heart (Sina, 16 December 2025) reports that Li Yan's team at Tangdu Hospital and Zhu Rui's team at Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute built CA-GPT. It says that they used open-source DeepSeek with retrieval over a million cardiovascular papers, on a Vivolight OCT platform. That description of the retrieval differs from the preprint's Methods. As of 29 October 2026, no source reports a peer-reviewed version or an independent evaluation.
purpose: CA-GPT was built to interpret intravascular OCT images and generate PCI planning and assessment decisions as expert-level support. The reported agreement with expert records is that purpose.

latest_review.limitations: The preprint’s claimed November 2023 release and October 2023 knowledge cutoff are inconsistent with the identified R1 family. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B is the likely checkpoint given the 14B parameter count, but the COMPARE authors provide no unambiguous repository or checkpoint identifier. The former DeepSeek release-announcement URL now returns the general API guide; that announcement was not read.
latest_review.origin_chain: COMPARE authors’ original arXiv preprint, reached from the retained abstract URL; checkpoint description checked against DeepSeek’s official model table and developer-owned repository metadata. The developer paper’s submission history supplies additional chronology.

display.answer: The account rests on the authors' arXiv preprint, which Machine Heart's article of 16 December 2025 retells. The OECD Monitor entry pairs the study with an unrelated Xinhua report on the “Titian” ablation robot. DeepSeek's own pages document the base model. The authors give no checkpoint identifier. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B is the likely checkpoint, given its 14 billion parameters.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: In a preprint on 96 patients, CA-GPT, built on DeepSeek-R1, agreed with expert stent plans more often than junior physicians and ChatGPT-5, which received only extracted measurements.
fields.account: An arXiv preprint of 11 December 2025 (Fang et al., last author Yan Li) reports the single-center COMPARE study. The study was retrospective and covered patients treated at Tangdu Hospital between June 2024 and August 2025. It compared CA-GPT, “a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system”, with ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) guided by optical coherence tomography (OCT). The preprint states that the large model layer is built on DeepSeek-R1 with 14 billion parameters. Its Methods describe retrieval from more than 100,000 annotated PCI cases and clinical guidance. The authors thank Vivolight Medtech for interface support and training. Decisions for 96 patients were scored against an expert-derived record. In pre-PCI planning CA-GPT's median agreement was 5 against 3 for ChatGPT-5 and 4 for junior physicians. It “showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01)”. CA-GPT received raw OCT images through its integrated pipeline, whereas ChatGPT-5 received manually extracted measurements. The comparison therefore combines differences in models, retrieval and input processing. The OECD Monitor pairs this study with a Xinhua report of 13 December 2025 on the “Titian” ablation robot at Shaoxing People's Hospital. That report describes teleoperation and no AI function. Machine Heart (Sina, 16 December 2025) reports that Li Yan's team at Tangdu Hospital and Zhu Rui's team at Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute built CA-GPT. It says that they used open-source DeepSeek with retrieval over a million cardiovascular papers, on a Vivolight OCT platform. That description of the retrieval differs from the preprint's Methods. As of 29 October 2026, no source reports a peer-reviewed version or an independent evaluation.
